filename: Improving Representations of Ice Crystals in Atmospheric Models_ Insights from in situ Imagery and Machine Learning.pdf
title: Improving Representations of Ice Crystals in Atmospheric Models: Insights from in situ Imagery and Machine Learning
venue: ELLIIT Focus Period Linköping 2024: Machine Learning for Climate Science
parameterization_target: ice crystal 3-D properties (surface area, effective density, habit)
testbed_rationale: Presentation slides with ongoing work; datasets and model codes are not yet publicly distributed with persistent links or benchmarks.
pain_points: Lack of 3-D ground truth observations of ice crystals requires relying on synthetic geometric models
Single-view object 3-D reconstruction often acts like classification rather than true reconstruction
Disentangling and structuring latent representations of ice crystal morphology without manual labels
Large structural differences between bulk and Lagrangian microphysics schemes make direct model comparison difficult
extraction_notes: The document is a slide presentation delivered at the ELLIIT Focus Period Linköping 2024 workshop on Machine Learning for Climate Science.
